tagline: Bringing Quality and Safety to Life
hero_kpi_rationale: Organic growth is the primary performance indicator in the TIC sector, reflecting the ability to gain market share and maintain structural demand in global supply chains.

kpis.name: Organic growth
kpis.explanation: Revenue growth excluding currency effects and acquisitions, shows real business performance.
kpis.description: Organic growth improved in 2015, driven by stable demand in industrial and commercial sectors.
kpis.signal: Positive organic growth in 2015, sign of solid demand.

kpis.name: Adjusted operating margin
kpis.explanation: Profit margin after adjustments, measures operational efficiency.
kpis.description: Adjusted operating margin progresses thanks to good cost discipline despite a difficult macroeconomic environment.

kpis.name: Adjusted EPS
kpis.explanation: Earnings per share after adjustments, measures shareholder profitability.
kpis.description: Adjusted EPS increases by 6.5%, supported by margin and organic growth.
kpis.signal: EPS growth in line with dividends.

kpis.name: Cash conversion
kpis.explanation: Ratio of adjusted operating cash flow to adjusted operating profit.
kpis.description: Cash conversion reaches 136.4%, well above 100%, thanks to rigorous working capital management.
kpis.signal: Very strong conversion, sign of cash-flow quality.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.explanation: Amount of dividend paid per share, in pence.
kpis.description: Total dividend per share increases by 6.5%, reflecting confidence in cash-flow generation.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group.
kpis.description: 41,400 employees at end 2015, with a large proportion in laboratories and on-site client offices.
kpis.signal: High headcount reflecting a service-oriented model.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 declared fiscal years by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 159.9 GBp last year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 declared fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 0.252 bn GBp last year.

kpis.name: Payout ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio: Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 73.4% last year.

risks.title: Reputation damage from ethical or quality misconduct
risks.score_rationale: Listed first among principal risks (position #1 in report), strong language ('destruction of shareholder value', 'zero-tolerance approach'). Risk stable but central to Intertek's TIC model. Reputation category is the very foundation of the certification/inspection business.

risks.title: Customer loss from customer service failure
risks.score_rationale: Risk #2 in filing, associated with multiple viability scenarios (customer service issue scenario). Moderate language ('gradual erosion', 'impact on quality'). Stable in 2025. High weight because competitive differentiation in TIC rests on service quality and responsiveness.

risks.title: Retention and attraction of specialized talent
risks.score_rationale: Risk #3 explicitly listed, mentioned in three of four viability scenarios. Direct language ('failure to optimise growth', 'poor management succession'). Stable but with strengthened HR strategies in 2025. Critical in a sector requiring accredited technical experts.

risks.title: Cyberattack and data security breach
risks.score_rationale: Risk #7, constitutes one of four viability scenarios ('IT systems or data security breach'). Strong language ('significant financial penalty', 'regulatory sanctions and potential fines'). Stable in 2025 but structurally growing risk in TIC sector handling confidential client data.

risks.title: Competitive landscape evolution and sector disruption
risks.score_rationale: Risk #6, explicitly linked to AI, new regulations and new business models. Forward-looking language ('radically new and different business models', 'failure to foresee'). Stable in 2025. High weight as TIC sector is transforming with test digitalization and emergence of new tech entrants.

risks.title: Ethical and regulatory non-compliance (anti-corruption, competition)
risks.score_rationale: Risk #10, listed as major legal and regulatory risk. Strong language ('significant fines and debarment from certain territories/activities', 'loss of accreditation'). Stable in 2025 with annual compliance confirmations. Particularly sensitive for Intertek operating in ~100 countries with varying anti-corruption legislation.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks impacting global operations
risks.score_rationale: Risk #9, constitutes one of four viability scenarios. Explicit mention of expanding sanctions lists (UK, EU, US, Australia in Q4 2025). Moderate language but trend toward increased monitoring. Risk stable but global geopolitical context in tension.

risks.title: Employee health, safety and well-being in field operations
risks.score_rationale: Risk #5, operational and legal category. Direct language ('avoiding fatalities, accidents and hazardous situations is paramount'). Stable in 2025. Particularly relevant for Intertek whose inspectors work in risky environments (factories, construction sites, chemical laboratories).

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or connected technologies in the 2015 annual report. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever during this period.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning or advanced automation in the document.
Cited innovations relate to inspection and certification processes, not digital technology.
Complete absence of AI-related vocabulary or initiatives in segments or risks.
